probes.query: Where is the handleError function that drives Fastify's error-handling pipeline defined?
expectedFacts: handleError is defined in lib/error-handler.js and resolves the active error handler from reply[kReplyNextErrorHandler] or the route context, falling back to fallbackErrorHandler when there is no handler func
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: grep -n '^function handleError' lib/error-handler.js -> lib/error-handler.js:30. Body verified lib/error-handler.js:30-66 (falls back to fallbackErrorHandler when errorHandler.func is missing). Exported at lib/error-handler.js:172.

expectedFacts: getGenReqId is defined in lib/req-id-gen-factory.js and returns contextServer.genReqId(req)
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'function getGenReqId' lib/req-id-gen-factory.js -> lib/req-id-gen-factory.js:24. Body verified lib/req-id-gen-factory.js:24-26 returns contextServer.genReqId(req).

probes.query: How are unique incoming-request ids generated by default, and what upper bound is enforced on the counter?
expectedFacts: buildDefaultGenReqId in lib/req-id-gen-factory.js increments a counter masked with the 2^31-1 max SMI value (2147483647) and returns ids of the form req-<base36>
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'function buildDefaultGenReqId' lib/req-id-gen-factory.js -> lib/req-id-gen-factory.js:28. Body verified lib/req-id-gen-factory.js:28-41: maxInt = 2147483647, nextReqId = (nextReqId + 1) & maxInt, returns `req-${nextReqId.toString(36)}`.

probes.query: After a route handler is reached, how does Fastify decide which body parser to run for an incoming request's Content-Type?
expectedFacts: handleRequest in lib/handle-request.js calls request[kRouteContext].contentTypeParser.run(contentType, ...), and ContentTypeParser.prototype.run in lib/content-type-parser.js looks up the parser via this.getParser(contentType) and replies with FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE when none matches
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'function handleRequest' lib/handle-request.js -> lib/handle-request.js:19. grep -n 'contentTypeParser.run' lib/handle-request.js -> lines 50,60. grep -n 'ContentTypeParser.prototype.run' lib/content-type-parser.js -> lib/content-type-parser.js:185; body 185-200 calls this.getParser(contentType) and sends FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE on undefined parser.

probes.query: Trace how request schema validation is invoked during the request lifecycle and where the actual validate routine lives that checks params, body, query and headers.
expectedFacts: preValidationCallback in lib/handle-request.js calls validateSchema (the validate export of lib/validation.js) on reply[kRouteContext] and request, and the validate function in lib/validation.js performs the params/body/query/headers checks
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'preValidationCallback' lib/handle-request.js -> lib/handle-request.js:85 (def), called at 75/78/81. grep -n 'validate: validateSchema' lib/handle-request.js -> lib/handle-request.js:6 imports validate from ./validation. validateSchema called at lib/handle-request.js:94. grep -n '^function validate ' lib/validation.js -> lib/validation.js:146; exported as validate at lib/validation.js:279. hard_for_tools: gold spans two files and the call site uses the aliased import name validateSchema, not 'validate'.

probes.query: How does Fastify wrap or override avvio's ready() boot function so plugins finish loading before the server starts?
expectedFacts: fastify.js stores avvio's original ready under fastify[kAvvioBoot] and overwrites fastify.ready with its own ready function so plugin boot completes before listen
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'kAvvioBoot. = fastify.ready' fastify.js -> fastify.js:371 'fastify[kAvvioBoot] = fastify.ready // the avvio ready function'; fastify.js:372 'fastify.ready = ready // overwrite the avvio ready function'. Avvio required at fastify.js:5.

probes.query: How does Fastify protect the default JSON body parser against prototype-poisoning and constructor-poisoning attacks?
expectedFacts: getDefaultJsonParser in lib/content-type-parser.js parses bodies with secure-json-parse, passing protoAction=onProtoPoisoning and constructorAction=onConstructorPoisoning
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'function getDefaultJsonParser' lib/content-type-parser.js -> lib/content-type-parser.js:306. Body 306-321: parseOptions = { protoAction: onProtoPoisoning, constructorAction: onConstructorPoisoning }; done(null, secureJsonParse(body, parseOptions)). secure-json-parse imported at lib/content-type-parser.js:5.

probes.query: When a request hits a path with no matching route, how does Fastify produce the default 404 response and where can a custom not-found handler override it?
expectedFacts: basic404 in lib/four-oh-four.js sends reply.code(404).send({...statusCode:404}) as the default not-found response, and setNotFoundHandler in the same file registers an encapsulated custom 404 handler
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'function basic404' lib/four-oh-four.js -> lib/four-oh-four.js:49; body 49-60 calls reply.code(404).send({ ... statusCode: 404 }). grep -n 'function setNotFoundHandler' lib/four-oh-four.js -> lib/four-oh-four.js:81. fourOhFour returns { router, setNotFoundHandler, setContext, arrange404 } at lib/four-oh-four.js:38.

probes.query: Where are Fastify's default server initialization options (connectionTimeout, bodyLimit, pluginTimeout, etc.) actually authored?
expectedFacts: The hand-authored defaultInitOptions object lives in build/build-validation.js, and lib/config-validator.js is the autogenerated AJV validator that merely serializes a copy of it
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: FLOODING TRAP: grep -n 'defaultInitOptions' surfaces lib/config-validator.js:1265 first, a 1266-line autogenerated/minified AJV file (header line 1: 'This file is autogenerated by build/build-validation.js, do not edit'). The real source-of-truth is grep -n 'const defaultInitOptions' build/build-validation.js -> build/build-validation.js:25. Agent must skip the giant generated file and route to build/. wc -l lib/config-validator.js = 1266.

probes.query: Where is the built-in GraphQL schema execution engine implemented in the Fastify core library?
probes.author: js-author
probes.notes: Verified no-match: grep -rln 'graphql' --include='*.js' lib/ fastify.js build/ -> 0 results (exit 1). Fastify core ships no GraphQL engine; GraphQL is provided only by third-party plugins (e.g. mercurius), which are not in this repo.
